correctness.rationale: The binary greedy-first-occurrence recursion proves exact shortest absent length and count. Its option-distance difference has only three states. An exact 12-cell transfer table over the four explicit length-16 blocks preserves equal counts, multiplies them by 2^(delta-min-4), and fixes the final difference away from zero; multiplication proves the arbitrary-block theorem. Binary-digit decomposition identifies the Rudin–Shapiro block morphism, and a paired-edge parity recurrence E(2q)=-E(q)-1 yields the all-rank index and count. The standalone embedded checker independently runs the table updates, direct next-occurrence DP, all 340 block concatenations up to four blocks, and ranks 4..13. Brute force also checked binary subsequence presence at ranks 4 and 5. Boundary k=4 is explicit; finite tests are evidence, not the infinite proof.
